system:
You are the Met office reviewer, standing in for the national meteorological centre (hazard facts). You check that the alert says what the hazard bulletin says: the same hazard, the same times, the same places, severity and certainty no higher or lower than the bulletin supports, and no unverified report in the alert.
You see only the event inputs (marked verified or unverified) and the English alert fields. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

data.summary: The only verified input is an internal no-notice drill message bracketed by 'Exercise, Exercise, Exercise'. The alert instead tells the public that a ballistic missile is inbound, with status Actual, certainty Observed and severity Extreme, and it says 'THIS IS NOT A DRILL'. No verified hazard supports any of these fields. Issuing this would be a false public missile alert, the January 2018 Hawaii failure mode. A person must stop this message and decide whether anything should go out at all.

objections.issue: The hazard is not supported by any verified input. The only verified source describes an internal drill message, not an observed or forecast missile threat. The headline and description assert a real inbound ballistic missile.
objections.fix: Do not issue a public missile warning. A responsible official must confirm whether any real hazard exists. If it does not, this message must not be sent to the public.

evidence.quote: No-notice internal drill message played by phone to the State Warning Point.
BALLISTIC MISSILE THREAT INBOUND TO HAWAII.
both before and after the message to indicate that it was a drill

objections.issue: The status is Actual, which means actionable by all recipients. The input is a drill, so at most it should be Exercise, actionable only by designated participants and carrying an exercise identifier in the note.
objections.fix: If the message is used at all, set status to Exercise, add the exercise identifier in note, and restrict distribution to exercise participants. Do not distribute it to the public.

evidence.quote: Actionable only by designated exercise participants; exercise identifier should appear in
No-notice internal drill message played by phone to the State Warning Point.

objections.issue: The phrase 'THIS IS NOT A DRILL' came from a scripting deviation inside the drill message. It does not confirm a real event. Certainty Observed, severity Extreme and urgency Immediate therefore have no basis in the verified input.
objections.fix: Remove 'THIS IS NOT A DRILL'. Do not assign Observed/Extreme/Immediate unless a verified bulletin confirms a real hazard.
